title.zh: 卷二十七 唐臣傳第十五: 朱弘昭 劉延朗 康思立 康義誠 藥彥稠
title.en: Volume 27 Later Tang Biographies 7: Zhu Hongzhao, Liu Yanlang, Kang Sili, Kang Yicheng, Yao Yanchou
title.raw: 卷二十七 唐臣傳第十五: 朱弘昭 劉延朗 康思立 康義誠 藥彥稠 Volume 27 Later Tang Biographies 7: Zhu Hongzhao, Liu Yanlang, Kang Sili, Kang Yicheng, Yao Yanchou

sentences.zh: 朱弘昭

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhao
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhao

sentences.zh: （馮赟附）〉

translations.literal: (With Feng Yun appended)〉
translations.idiomatic: (With Feng Yun appended)〉

sentences.zh: 朱弘昭，太原人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhao was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhao came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少事明宗為客將，明宗即位，為文思使。

translations.literal: In youth he served Mingzong as a guest officer; when Mingzong took the throne, he became commissioner of the Bureau of Literary Thought.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served Mingzong as a guest officer. When Mingzong became emperor, he was made commissioner of the Bureau of Literary Thought.

sentences.zh: 與安重誨有隙，故常使於外。

translations.literal: He was at odds with An Chonghui, so he was often sent on missions abroad.
translations.idiomatic: He feuded with An Chonghui and was therefore kept on duty outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 董璋為東川節度使，乃以弘昭為副使。

translations.literal: When Dong Chuan was military governor of Dongchuan, Hongzhao was made his deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chuan held Dongchuan as military governor; Hongzhao was appointed his deputy.

sentences.zh: 西川孟知祥殺其監軍李嚴，弘昭大懼，求還京師，璋不許，遂相猜忌，弘昭益開懷待之不疑，璋頗重其為人。

translations.literal: In Xichuan Meng Zhixiang killed the army supervisor Li Yan. Hongzhao was greatly afraid and asked to return to the capital, but Zhang would not allow it. They grew mutually suspicious. Hongzhao then opened his heart and treated Zhang without suspicion, and Zhang came to respect his character.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang of Xichuan killed the army supervisor Li Yan. Hongzhao was terrified and begged to return to court, but Dong Chuan refused. Suspicion grew between them—yet Hongzhao treated him openly and without mistrust, and Zhang came to respect him.

sentences.zh: 後璋有軍事，遣弘昭入朝，弘昭乃免。

translations.literal: Later, when Zhang had military affairs, he sent Hongzhao to court on tribute duty, and Hongzhao thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Later Dong Chuan sent him to court on official business, and Hongzhao was able to leave.

sentences.zh: 遷左衛大將軍內客省使、宣徽南院使、鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand General of the Left Guard, commissioner of the Inner Service Bureau, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, and military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand General of the Left Guard, commissioner of the Inner Service Bureau and of the Southern Palace Secretariat, and military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥反，石敬瑭伐蜀，久無功，明宗遣安重誨督軍。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang rebelled; Shi Jingtang campaigned against Shu without success for a long time. Mingzong sent An Chonghui to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Zhixiang rebelled, Shi Jingtang’s campaign against Shu dragged on without success. Mingzong sent An Chonghui to take charge of the army.

sentences.zh: 是時重誨已有間。

translations.literal: By then Chonghui was already estranged from the throne.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chonghui had already fallen from favor.

sentences.zh: 重誨至鳳翔，弘昭迎謁，禮甚恭，延重誨於家，使其妻妾侍飲食。

translations.literal: When Chonghui reached Fengxiang, Hongzhao went out to meet him with great courtesy, entertained him at home, and had his wife and concubines serve food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui reached Fengxiang. Hongzhao received him with elaborate courtesy, entertained him at home, and had his household serve the meal.

sentences.zh: 重誨以弘昭厚己，酒酣，具言蒙天子厚恩，而所以讒間之端，因泣下。

translations.literal: Because Hongzhao had treated him generously, when the wine was deep Chonghui spoke at length of the emperor’s great grace toward him and of the origins of the slander that had set them at odds, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao had been lavish toward him. Deep in wine, Chonghui spoke of the emperor’s kindness and of how slander had come between them—and wept.

sentences.zh: 弘昭即奏言重誨怨望，又陰遣人馳告敬瑭，使拒重誨。

translations.literal: Hongzhao immediately memorialized that Chonghui harbored resentment, and also secretly sent men in haste to tell Jingtang to resist Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao at once reported that Chonghui was disaffected, and secretly sent riders to urge Jingtang to defy him.

sentences.zh: 會敬瑭以糧餉不繼，遽燒營返軍。

translations.literal: Just then Jingtang, because provisions would not follow, suddenly burned the camps and turned the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang’s supplies failed; he burned the camps and marched home.

sentences.zh: 重誨亦以被讒召還，過鳳翔，弘昭閉門不納，重誨由此得罪死。

translations.literal: Chonghui too was recalled because of slander. Passing Fengxiang, Hongzhao shut his gates and would not admit him. From this Chonghui was condemned and died.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui was recalled on charges of disloyalty. At Fengxiang, Hongzhao shut him out. That was how Chonghui fell and died.

sentences.zh: 樞密使範延光尤惡弘昭為人，罷為左武衛上將軍、宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Fan Yanguang especially hated Hongzhao’s character and had him demoted to Senior General of the Left Martial Guard and commissioner of the Southern Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang, chief councillor, detested Hongzhao and had him reduced to Senior General of the Left Martial Guard and commissioner of the Southern Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 久之，為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: After a long while he became military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made military governor of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 是時，明宗已病，而秦王從榮禍起有端，唐諸大臣皆欲引去以避禍。

translations.literal: By then Mingzong was already ill, and trouble with the Prince of Qin, Congrong, was beginning to show. The great ministers of Tang all wished to withdraw to avoid disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was ill, and the Prince of Qin Congrong’s rebellion was taking shape. Tang’s senior ministers all wanted to leave court to escape what was coming.

sentences.zh: 樞密使範延光、趙延壽日夕更見，涕泣求去，明宗怒而不許。

translations.literal: Chief councillors Fan Yanguang and Zhao Yanshou saw the emperor day and night in turn, weeping and begging to go; Mingzong was angry and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang and Zhao Yanshou pleaded day and night, weeping to be released; Mingzong refused in anger.

sentences.zh: 延壽使其妻興平公主入言於中，延光亦因孟漢瓊、王淑妃進說，故皆得罷。

translations.literal: Yanshou had his wife, the Princess of Xingping, speak within the palace; Yanguang also advanced his case through Meng Hanqiong and Consort Wang. Thus both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou’s wife, the Princess of Xingping, pleaded inside the palace; Yanguang won the same through Meng Hanqiong and Consort Wang. Both left office.

sentences.zh: 以弘昭及馮赟代延壽、延光，弘昭入見，辭曰：「臣廝養之才，不足當大任。

translations.literal: Hongzhao and Feng Yun replaced Yanshou and Yanguang. When Hongzhao came to audience he declined, saying: “Your servant has only the talent of a menial—unfit for great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao and Feng Yun took their places. Hongzhao appeared and declined: “I am only menial stock—unfit for such a post.

sentences.zh: 」明宗叱之曰：「公等皆不欲在吾目前邪？

translations.literal: ” Mingzong rebuked him: “Do you gentlemen all refuse to stay before my eyes?
translations.idiomatic: ” Mingzong snapped: “Do you all refuse to remain in my sight?

sentences.zh: 吾養公等安用！

translations.literal: What use are you to me if I keep you!
translations.idiomatic: What use are you to me then!

sentences.zh: 」弘昭惶恐，乃視事。

translations.literal: ” Hongzhao was afraid and took up his duties.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hongzhao, terrified, accepted the post.

sentences.zh: 馮赟者，亦太原人也。

translations.literal: Feng Yun was also a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yun too came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 其父璋，事明宗為閽者。

translations.literal: His father Zhang had served Mingzong as a gatekeeper.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang had been a gatekeeper in Mingzong’s service.

sentences.zh: 赟為兒時，以通黠為明宗所愛。

translations.literal: When Yun was a boy, his cleverness won Mingzong’s affection.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Yun’s quick wit won Mingzong’s favor.

sentences.zh: 明宗為節度使，以赟為進奏官。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was military governor, he made Yun his memorial courier.
translations.idiomatic: While Mingzong was still a military governor, he made Yun his memorial courier.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，即為客省使、宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Yun at once became commissioner of the Guest Bureau and of the Northern Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingzong’s accession Yun became commissioner of the Guest Bureau and of the Northern Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 歷河東忠武節度使、三司使。

translations.literal: He served successively as military governor of Hedong and Zhongwu and as commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Hedong and Zhongwu and headed the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 明宗病甚，大臣稀復進見，而孟漢瓊、王淑妃用事，弘昭及赟並掌機務於中，大事皆決此四人。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was gravely ill, ministers rarely saw him again. Meng Hanqiong and Consort Wang held power. Hongzhao and Yun together handled affairs within the palace, and all great matters were decided by these four.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong lay dying; ministers seldom gained audience. Meng Hanqiong and Consort Wang ran affairs. Hongzhao and Yun held the inner councils, and these four decided everything of weight.

sentences.zh: 及殺秦王而立湣帝，益自以為功。

translations.literal: After they killed the Prince of Qin and enthroned Emperor Min, they thought their merit still greater.
translations.idiomatic: After killing the Prince of Qin and raising Emperor Min, they counted the deed their greatest triumph.

sentences.zh: 又其所用多非其人，給事中陳乂，為人險譎，好陰謀，嘗事梁張漢傑，又事郭崇韜，兩人皆輒敗死，弘昭乃引以為樞密直學士，而用其謀。

translations.literal: Moreover, those they employed were often unworthy. The supervisory attendant Chen Yi was treacherous and fond of secret plots. He had served Zhang Hanjie of Liang and Guo Chongtao; both men had promptly met ruin and death. Hongzhao nevertheless brought him in as a direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and used his schemes.
translations.idiomatic: They staffed posts with the wrong men. Chen Yi, a supervisory attendant, was devious and loved intrigue. He had served Zhang Hanjie of Liang and Guo Chongtao—both destroyed. Hongzhao still made him a direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 是時，弘昭、赟遣漢瓊至魏，召湣帝入立，而留漢瓊權知後事。

translations.literal: At that time Hongzhao and Yun sent Hanqiong to Wei to summon Emperor Min to take the throne, leaving Hanqiong to manage affairs in the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao and Yun sent Hanqiong to Wei to bring Emperor Min to the throne, with Hanqiong left to govern in their absence.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，漢瓊請入朝，弘昭、赟乃議徙成德範延光代漢瓊，北京留守石敬瑭代延光，鳳翔潞王從珂代敬瑭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Hanqiong asked to come to court. Hongzhao and Yun then planned to move Fan Yanguang of Chengde to replace Hanqiong, the northern capital’s regent Shi Jingtang to replace Yanguang, and the Prince of Lu Congke of Fengxiang to replace Jingtang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year’s first month, Hanqiong sought audience. Hongzhao and Yun proposed shifting Fan Yanguang from Chengde into Hanqiong’s post, Shi Jingtang from the northern capital into Fan’s, and the Prince of Lu Congke from Fengxiang into Jingtang’s.

sentences.zh: 三人者皆唐大臣，以漢瓊故，輕易其地，又不降制書，第遣使者監其上道，從珂由此遂反。

translations.literal: All three were great ministers of Tang. Because of Hanqiong they were moved lightly from their posts, and no imperial edict was issued—only envoys were sent to supervise their departure on the road. From this Congke rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: All three were senior Tang ministers. For Hanqiong’s sake their commands were swapped casually, without formal edicts—only escorts hurried them on the road. Congke rebelled because of it.

sentences.zh: 從珂兵已東，湣帝大懼，遣人召弘昭計事。

translations.literal: Congke’s army was already marching east. Emperor Min was greatly afraid and sent men to summon Hongzhao to counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Congke’s host was eastward bound. Emperor Min, terrified, sent for Hongzhao.

sentences.zh: 弘昭謂其客穆延暉曰：「上召我急，將罪我也。

translations.literal: Hongzhao told his retainer Mu Yanhui: “The emperor summons me in haste—he means to punish me.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao told his client Mu Yanhui: “The emperor calls me urgently. He means to blame me.

sentences.zh: 吾兒婦，君之女也，其以歸，無使及禍。

translations.literal: My son’s wife is your daughter—take her home and do not let her share the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: My daughter-in-law is your daughter. Take her away—do not let her be caught in this.

sentences.zh: 」乃拔劍大哭，欲自裁，而家人止之。

translations.literal: ” He drew his sword and wept aloud, wishing to kill himself, but his household stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He drew his sword, wept, and tried to take his life; his family restrained him.

sentences.zh: 使者促弘昭入見甚急，弘昭呼曰：「窮至此邪！

translations.literal: The envoy pressed him to enter audience with great urgency. Hongzhao cried: “Driven to this extremity!
translations.idiomatic: The messenger hurried him to court. Hongzhao shouted: “Brought to this pass!

sentences.zh: 」乃自投於井以死。

translations.literal: ” Then he threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: ” He threw himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 安從進聞之，亦殺赟於家，赟母新死，子母棄屍於道，妻子皆見殺。

translations.literal: When An Congjin heard of it, he also killed Yun at his home. Yun’s mother had just died; mother and son were left dead in the road. Wife and children were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: An Congjin heard and killed Yun at home. Yun’s mother had just died; their bodies were cast into the street. Wife and children perished with him.

sentences.zh: 赟有子三歲，其故吏張守素匿之以免。

translations.literal: Yun had a three-year-old son; his former clerk Zhang Shousu hid the child and saved him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun’s son was three. His old clerk Zhang Shousu hid the boy and spared him.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖即位，贈弘昭尚書令，赟中書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne, Hongzhao was posthumously made Grand Secretary and Yun made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Later Han posthumously made Hongzhao Grand Secretary and Yun Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 劉延朗

translations.literal: Liu Yanlang
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanlang

sentences.zh: 帝既立，以昭胤為左諫議大夫、端明殿學士，專美為比部郎中、樞密院直學士，審虔為皇城使，暠為宣徽北院使，延朗為莊宅使。

translations.literal: After the emperor took the throne, Zhao Yinchao was made Left Remonstrator and academician of the Duanming Hall; Zhu Mei was made director of the Bureau of Revenue and direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Shen Qian was made commissioner of the Imperial City; Hao was made commissioner of the Northern Palace Secretariat; Yanlang was made commissioner of the Imperial Estates.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, the emperor made Zhao Yinchao Left Remonstrator and Duanming academician; Zhu Mei director of the Bureau of Revenue and direct academician of Military Affairs; Shen Qian commissioner of the Imperial City; Hao commissioner of the Northern Palace Secretariat; and Yanlang commissioner of the Imperial Estates.

sentences.zh: 久之，昭胤、暠為樞密使，延朗為副使，審虔為侍衛步軍都指揮使，而薛文遇亦為職方郎中、樞密院直學士。

translations.literal: After a long while Zhao Yinchao and Hao became chief councillors, Yanlang became deputy chief councillor, Shen Qian became commander of the Palace Foot Guards, and Xue Wenyu also became director of the Bureau of Appointments and direct academician of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In time Zhao Yinchao and Hao became chief councillors, Yanlang deputy, Shen Qian commander of the palace foot guards, and Xue Wenyu director of Appointments and direct academician of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 由是審虔將兵，專美、文遇主謀議，而昭胤、暠及延朗掌機密。

translations.literal: Thus Shen Qian commanded troops; Zhu Mei and Wenyu led counsel; and Zhao Yinchao, Hao, and Yanlang held the secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qian held the armies; Zhu Mei and Wenyu shaped policy; Zhao Yinchao, Hao, and Yanlang held the confidential seals.

sentences.zh: 初，帝與晉高祖俱事明宗，而心不相悅。

translations.literal: At first the emperor and the High Ancestor of Jin had both served Mingzong, but their hearts were not fond of each other.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and the Jin High Ancestor had both served Mingzong, yet they never liked each other.

sentences.zh: 帝既入立，高祖不得已來朝，而心頗自疑，欲求歸鎮，且難言之，乃陽為羸疾，灸灼滿身，冀帝憐而遣之。

translations.literal: After the emperor entered the throne, the High Ancestor had no choice but to come to court, yet he was full of suspicion. He wished to return to his command but found it hard to say so. He feigned wasting illness and burned moxa over his whole body, hoping the emperor would pity him and send him away.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, the emperor compelled the High Ancestor to attend court. Jingtang came, uneasy and eager to return to his post. Unable to speak plainly, he pretended grave illness and covered himself with moxa burns, hoping pity would send him home.

sentences.zh: 延朗等多言敬瑭可留京師，昭胤、專美曰：「敬瑭與趙延壽皆尚唐公主，不可獨留。

translations.literal: Yanlang and the others often said Jingtang could be kept in the capital. Zhao Yinchao and Zhu Mei said: “Jingtang and Zhao Yanshou have both married Tang princesses—they cannot be detained alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang’s faction urged keeping Jingtang in the capital. Zhao Yinchao and Zhu Mei objected: “Jingtang and Zhao Yanshou both married Tang princesses. You cannot hold one and not the other.

sentences.zh: 」乃復授高祖河東而遣之。

translations.literal: ” They then reappointed the High Ancestor to Hedong and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: ” So the High Ancestor was sent back to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 是時，契丹數寇北邊，以高祖為大同、振武、威塞、彰國等軍蕃漢馬步軍都總管，屯於忻州。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan raided the northern border repeatedly. The High Ancestor was made overall commander of Tangut and Han horse and foot of the Datong, Zhenwu, Weisai, Zhangguo, and other armies, stationed at Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan raids pressed the north. Jingtang was made overall commander of Tangut and Han forces of Datong, Zhenwu, Weisai, Zhangguo, and other commands, encamped at Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 而屯兵忽變，擁高祖呼「萬歲」，高祖懼，斬三十餘人而後止。

translations.literal: Suddenly the encamped troops mutinied, surrounded the High Ancestor, and shouted “Long live!” He was afraid and beheaded more than thirty men before they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His troops mutinied, surrounded him, and shouted “Long live!” He cut down thirty-odd men before order returned.

sentences.zh: 於是帝益疑之。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore suspected him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s suspicion deepened.

sentences.zh: 是時，高祖悉握精兵在北，饋運芻糧，遠近勞弊。

translations.literal: At that time the High Ancestor held elite troops in the north in his grasp; fodder and grain were transported from afar, and the realm was worn out.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang held the best troops in the north; supply lines stretched far and exhausted the country.

sentences.zh: 帝與延朗等日夕謀議，而專美、文遇叠宿中興殿盧，召見訪問，常至夜分而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor and Yanlang and the others plotted day and night, while Zhu Mei and Wenyu lodged night after night in the Zhongxing Hall chambers and were summoned for counsel, often not dismissed until deep in the night.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor plotted with Yanlang day and night. Zhu Mei and Wenyu slept in the Zhongxing Hall and were called in for counsel, often until midnight.

sentences.zh: 是時，高祖弟重胤為皇城副使，而石氏公主母曹太后居中，因得伺帝動靜言語以報高祖，高祖益自危懼。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor’s younger brother Chongyin was deputy commissioner of the Imperial City. The Stone princess’s mother, Empress Dowager Cao, was within the palace. Thus they could watch the emperor’s movements and words and report to the High Ancestor, who grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang’s brother Chongyin was deputy commissioner of the Imperial City. The Stone princess’s mother, Dowager Cao, was inside the palace. They watched the emperor’s every move and word and reported to Jingtang, who grew more fearful still.

sentences.zh: 每帝遣使者勞軍，即陽為羸疾不自堪，因數求解總管以探帝心。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor sent envoys to comfort the army, he would feign wasting illness beyond endurance and repeatedly ask to be relieved of overall command to probe the emperor’s mind.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor sent envoys to the army, Jingtang played at collapse and begged again and again to be relieved of command—testing the throne’s intent.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝母魏氏追封宣憲皇太后，而墓在太原，有司議立寢宮。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor’s mother, the Wei clan, was posthumously titled Empress Dowager Xuanxian, and her tomb was at Taiyuan. The offices debated erecting a resting palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s mother, Lady Wei, was posthumously made Empress Dowager Xuanxian. Her tomb lay at Taiyuan, and the ministries debated building a palace there.

sentences.zh: 高祖建言陵與民家墓相雜，不可立宮。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor argued that the tomb was mixed among common graves and that no palace should be built.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang argued the tomb lay among commoners’ graves and that no palace should be raised.

sentences.zh: 帝疑高祖欲毀民墓，為國取怨，帝由此發怒，罷高祖總管，徙鄆州。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected the High Ancestor wished to destroy commoners’ graves and win the people’s hatred for the state. The emperor was enraged by this, removed the High Ancestor from overall command, and transferred him to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Jingtang meant to raze common graves and earn the realm’s hatred. Enraged, he stripped him of command and moved him to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 延朗等多言不可，而司天趙延義亦言天象失度，宜安靜以弭災，其事遂止。

translations.literal: Yanlang and the others often said it could not be done, and the Director of Astronomy Zhao Yanyi also said the heavens were out of measure and that quiet was needed to quell disaster. The matter then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang’s party objected; the Director of Astronomy Zhao Yanyi said the heavens were disturbed and the court should keep still. The transfer was dropped.

sentences.zh: 後月余，文遇獨直，帝夜召之，語罷敬瑭事，文遇曰：「臣聞『作舍道邊，三年不成』。

translations.literal: More than a month later Wenyu alone was on night duty. The emperor summoned him at night and, when talk ended on Jingtang’s affair, Wenyu said: “I have heard, ‘Build a house beside the road and in three years it is not finished.’”
translations.idiomatic: A month later Wenyu held night watch alone. The emperor called him at night. When they came to Jingtang, Wenyu said: “They say, ‘Build a house beside the road and in three years it is still unfinished.’”

sentences.zh: 國家之事，斷在陛下。

translations.literal: The affairs of the state are decided by Your Majesty alone.
translations.idiomatic: State affairs belong to Your Majesty alone.

sentences.zh: 且敬瑭徙亦反，不徙亦反，遲速爾，不如先事圖之。

translations.literal: Moreover, if Jingtang is moved he will rebel; if he is not moved he will rebel—the only question is sooner or later. Better to strike first.
translations.idiomatic: Move Jingtang and he rebels; leave him and he rebels—only the timing differs. Strike first.

sentences.zh: 」帝大喜曰：「術者言朕今年當得一賢佐以定天下，卿其是邪！

translations.literal: ” The emperor was greatly pleased and said: “The diviners said that this year I would gain one worthy assistant to settle the realm—is it you!
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor rejoiced: “Soothsayers said I would gain one worthy man this year to settle the realm—is it you!

sentences.zh: 」乃令文遇手書除目，夜半下學士院草制。

translations.literal: ” He had Wenyu write out the appointment order by hand, and at midnight sent it to the Academy to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had Wenyu write the appointment order himself and at midnight sent it to the Hanlin to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 明日宣制，文武兩班皆失色。

translations.literal: The next day the edict was proclaimed; both civil and military ranks turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the edict was read. Civil and military officials alike went white.

sentences.zh: 居五六日，敬瑭以反聞。

translations.literal: Within five or six days word came that Jingtang had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Within a week came word that Jingtang had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭上書，言帝非明宗子，而許王從益次當立。

translations.literal: Jingtang sent up a memorial saying the emperor was not Mingzong’s son and that Prince Xu Congyi was next in line for the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang’s memorial claimed the emperor was not Mingzong’s son and that Prince Xu Congyi should reign.

sentences.zh: 帝得書大怒，手壞而投之，召學士馬胤孫為答詔，曰：「宜以惡語詆之。」

translations.literal: The emperor received the letter, was furious, tore it apart with his hands and cast it away, and summoned the academician Ma Yinsun to draft a reply, saying: “Use harsh words to revile him.”.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it, flew into a rage, tore the letter apart, and summoned Ma Yinsun to answer: “Revile him in the vilest terms.”.

sentences.zh: 延朗等請帝親征，帝心憂懼，常惡言敬瑭事，每戒人曰：「爾無說石郎，令我心膽墮地！

translations.literal: Yanlang and the others asked the emperor to campaign in person. The emperor’s heart was anxious and afraid; he often spoke harshly of Jingtang’s affair and would warn people: “Do not speak of Lord Stone to me—my heart and guts drop to the ground!
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang urged a personal campaign. The emperor was sick with fear, could not bear talk of Jingtang, and warned his court: “Do not mention Lord Stone—I feel my heart fall through the floor!

sentences.zh: 」由此不欲行。

translations.literal: ” From this he did not wish to go.
translations.idiomatic: ” He did not want to march.

sentences.zh: 而延朗等屢迫之，乃行。

translations.literal: But Yanlang and the others pressed him again and again, and he went.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang pressed him until he went.

sentences.zh: 至懷州，帝夜召李崧問以計策。

translations.literal: Reaching Huaizhou, the emperor summoned Li Song at night to ask his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: At Huaizhou he called Li Song at night for counsel.

sentences.zh: 文遇不知而繼至，帝見之色變，崧躡其足，文遇乃出。

translations.literal: Wenyu did not know and followed in; when the emperor saw him his color changed. Song trod on his foot, and Wenyu went out.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu came in unaware. The emperor’s face changed. Song stepped on his foot; Wenyu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我見文遇肉顫，欲抽刀刺之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “When I see Wenyu my flesh trembles—I want to draw a knife and stab him.”.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: “I see Wenyu and my flesh crawls—I want to stab him.”.

sentences.zh: 」崧曰：「文遇小人，致誤大事，刺之益醜。

translations.literal: Song said: “Wenyu is a petty man who has ruined a great affair. To stab him would only add ugliness.”.
translations.idiomatic: Song said: “Wenyu is a petty man who has ruined everything. Stabbing him would only shame the throne.”.

sentences.zh: 」乃已。

translations.literal: ” He desisted.
translations.idiomatic: ” He let it go.

sentences.zh: 是時，契丹已立敬瑭為天子，以兵而南，帝惶惑不知所之。

translations.literal: By then the Khitan had already enthroned Jingtang as Son of Heaven and marched south with troops. The emperor was in panic and did not know where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had made Jingtang emperor and marched south. The emperor panicked, without a plan.

sentences.zh: 遣審虔將千騎至白馬坡踏戰地，審虔曰：「何地不堪戰？

translations.literal: He sent Shen Qian with a thousand horsemen to the White Horse Slope to reconnoiter the battlefield. Shen Qian said: “What ground is not fit for battle?
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shen Qian with a thousand horse to scout the White Horse Slope. Shen Qian said: “What ground cannot be fought?

sentences.zh: 雖有其地，何人肯立於此？

translations.literal: Even if there is such ground, who would stand here?
translations.idiomatic: Even if there were, who would stand here?

sentences.zh: 不如還也。

translations.literal: Better to turn back.”.
translations.idiomatic: Better turn back.”.

sentences.zh: 」帝遂還，自焚。

translations.literal: The emperor then returned and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned back and burned himself alive.

sentences.zh: 高祖入京師，延朗等六人皆除名為民。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor entered the capital, Yanlang and the other six men were all stripped of office and made commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang entered the capital. Yanlang and five others were demoted to commoners.

sentences.zh: 初，延朗與暠並掌機密，延朗專任事，諸將當得州者，不以功次為先後，納賂多者得善州，少及無賂者得惡州，或久而不得，由是人人皆怨。

translations.literal: At first Yanlang and Hao together held the secrets, but Yanlang monopolized affairs. Of the generals due to receive prefectures, merit was not the order of precedence—those who paid larger bribes received good prefectures; those who paid little or none received bad ones, or sometimes waited long without receiving any. From this everyone resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang and Hao had shared the secrets, but Yanlang ran everything. Generals awaiting commands bought their posts—heavy bribes won good provinces, light or none won bad ones, and some waited forever. Everyone hated him.

sentences.zh: 暠心患之，而不能爭也，但日飽食高枕而已。

translations.literal: Hao was troubled in heart but could not contend; he only ate his fill each day and slept with a high pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was uneasy but could not fight him. He ate well and slept with a high pillow.

sentences.zh: 每延朗議事，則垂頭陽睡不省。

translations.literal: Whenever Yanlang discussed affairs, he would hang his head and feign sleep, paying no attention.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yanlang met to discuss policy, Hao hung his head and pretended to sleep.

sentences.zh: 及晉兵入，延朗以一騎走南山，過其家，指而嘆曰：「吾積錢三十萬於此，不知何人取之！

translations.literal: When the Jin army entered, Yanlang fled south on a single horse. Passing his house he pointed and sighed: “I stored three hundred thousand cash here—who knows who will take it!
translations.idiomatic: When Jin troops entered, Yanlang fled south alone. At his house he pointed and sighed: “I piled three hundred thousand strings of cash here—who will take it now!

sentences.zh: 」遂為追兵所殺。

translations.literal: ” Pursuing troops killed him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Pursuers cut him down.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖聞暠常不與延朗事，哀之，後復以為將。

translations.literal: The Jin High Ancestor heard that Hao had often refused to join Yanlang’s schemes and pitied him; later he was again made a general.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin High Ancestor heard Hao had kept out of Yanlang’s plots and pitied him; later he was restored to command.

sentences.zh: 歲餘卒。

translations.literal: After a year more he died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died.

sentences.zh: 專美事晉為大理卿，開運中卒。

translations.literal: Zhu Mei served Jin as director of the Court of Judicial Review and died in the Kaiyun era.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei served Jin as director of the Court of Judicial Review and died in the Kaiyun period.

sentences.zh: 當晉之將起，廢帝以昭胤為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，出為河陽節度使，與審虔、文遇皆不知其所終。

translations.literal: When Jin was about to rise, the Deposed Emperor made Zhao Yinchao Vice Grand Councillor and co-signer of the Secretariat, then sent him out as military governor of Heyang. Together with Shen Qian and Wenyu, their ends are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: As Jin rose, the Deposed Emperor made Zhao Yinchao Vice Grand Councillor and sent him to govern Heyang. He, Shen Qian, and Wenyu vanish from the record.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，禍福成敗之理，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Alas—the principle of fortune and disaster, success and failure, is not to be ignored!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the logic of fortune and ruin is a lesson not to be ignored!

sentences.zh: 張濛神言驗矣，然焉知其不為禍也！

translations.literal: Zhang Meng’s spirit words came true—yet who could know they would not become disaster!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Meng’s oracle proved true—yet who could tell it would bring ruin as well!

sentences.zh: 予之所記，大抵如此，覽者可以深思焉。

translations.literal: What I have recorded is broadly of this kind; readers may ponder it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: What I have set down is roughly this; let readers weigh it carefully.

sentences.zh: 廢帝之起，所與圖議者，此五六人而已。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor rose, only these five or six men plotted with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to power, only these five or six men shaped the plot.

sentences.zh: 考其逆順之理，雖有智者為之謀，未必能不敗，況如此五六人者哉！

translations.literal: Examining the principle of compliance and rebellion, even if a wise man planned for them, he might not have escaped defeat—how much less such five or six men!
translations.idiomatic: Weigh their course against right and rebellion: even a wise counselor might not have saved them—what chance had men like these?

sentences.zh: 故並述以附延朗，見其始終之際云。

translations.literal: Therefore I narrate them together as an appendix to Yanlang, to show their beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: I tell their whole story here with Yanlang, from first rise to final fall.

sentences.zh: 康思立

translations.literal: Kang Sili
translations.idiomatic: Kang Sili

sentences.zh: 康思立，本山陰諸部人也。

translations.literal: Kang Sili was originally a man of the Shanyin tribal groups.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Sili came from the Shanyin tribal confederations.

sentences.zh: 少為騎將，從莊宗破梁夾城，戰柏鄉，累以功遷突騎指揮使。

translations.literal: In youth he was a cavalry officer. He followed Zhuangzong in breaking Liang’s Jia City and fighting at Baxiang, and was repeatedly promoted for merit to commander of the Vanguard Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: As a young cavalry officer he followed Zhuangzong at Jia City and Baxiang and rose for merit to command the Vanguard Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，歷應嵐二州刺史、宿州團練使、昭武軍節度使，徙鎮保義，皆有善政。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he served successively as prefect of Ying and Lan prefectures, regimental commissioner of Suzhou, and military governor of Zhaowu, then was transferred to govern Baoyi—all with good administration.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he governed Ying and Lan, commanded Suzhou’s regiments, and held Zhaowu and Baoyi with a reputation for good rule.

sentences.zh: 潞王從珂反於鳳翔，湣帝遣王思同等討之，思立有捧聖、羽林屯兵千五百人，乃以羽林千人屬思同。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu Congke rebelled at Fengxiang, Emperor Min sent Wang Sitong to suppress him. Sili had fifteen hundred men of the Sacred Support and Feathered Forest encampments and gave a thousand of the Feathered Forest to Sitong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu Congke rebelled at Fengxiang, Emperor Min sent Wang Sitong against him. Sili had fifteen hundred Sacred Support and Feathered Forest troops and lent Sitong a thousand of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 思同至鳳翔，軍叛，降於從珂。

translations.literal: Sitong reached Fengxiang; the army mutinied and surrendered to Congke.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong reached Fengxiang; his army mutinied and went over to Congke.

sentences.zh: 思立聞之，欲盡誅羽林千人家屬，未及，而從珂兵已至，思立乃以捧聖兵城守，從珂兵傅其城，呼曰：「西兵七萬策新天子，爾五百人其能拒邪？

translations.literal: Sili heard of it and wished to execute the families of the thousand Feathered Forest men, but before he could, Congke’s army arrived. Sili then held the city with the Sacred Support troops. Congke’s army pressed the walls and called: “Seventy thousand western soldiers have enthroned a new Son of Heaven—can your five hundred men resist?
translations.idiomatic: Sili meant to slaughter the families of the thousand mutineers, but Congke’s host was already there. He held the walls with the Sacred Support. Congke’s men shouted: “Seventy thousand western troops have raised a new emperor—can five hundred of you stand against them?

sentences.zh: 徒陷陜人於死耳！

translations.literal: You will only trap the people of Shaan into death!
translations.idiomatic: You will only bury the people of Shaan in slaughter!

sentences.zh: 」捧聖兵聞之，皆解甲，思立遂開門迎從珂。

translations.literal: When the Sacred Support troops heard this, they all laid down their armor. Sili then opened the gates and welcomed Congke.
translations.idiomatic: The Sacred Support heard and threw down their arms. Sili opened the gates and welcomed Congke in.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，以思立初無降意，頗不悅之，徙安遠，又徙安國，以年老罷為右神武統軍。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, because Sili at first had shown no intent to surrender, he was quite displeased and transferred him to Anyuan, then to Anguo, and finally dismissed him as Senior Commander of the Right Divine Martial Guard for old age.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor resented Sili’s first refusal to yield and moved him to Anyuan, then Anguo, then retired him as Senior Commander of the Right Divine Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭反太原，廢帝以思立為北面行營馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Shi Jingtang rebelled at Taiyuan, the Deposed Emperor made Sili overall commander of the northern campaign’s horse army.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jingtang rebelled at Taiyuan, the Deposed Emperor made Sili commander of the northern campaign’s cavalry.

sentences.zh: 廢帝幸懷州，遣思立將從駕騎兵出團柏谷救張敬達，未至，而敬達死，楊光遠降晉，思立疾，卒於道。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor went to Huaizhou and sent Sili with the accompanying cavalry out through Tuanbai Valley to rescue Zhang Jingda, but before he arrived Jingda was dead and Yang Guangyuan surrendered to Jin. Sili fell ill and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched to Huaizhou and sent Sili with the imperial escort through Tuanbai Valley to relieve Zhang Jingda. Jingda died first; Yang Guangyuan surrendered to Jin. Sili fell ill and died on the march.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖入立，贈太子少師。

translations.literal: When the Jin High Ancestor entered and took the throne, Sili was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang posthumously made him Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 康義誠

translations.literal: Kang Yicheng
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yicheng

sentences.zh: 秦王從榮素驕，自為河南尹，典六軍，拜大元帥，唐諸大臣皆懼禍及，思自脫，獨義誠心結之，遣其子事秦王府。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin Congrong had always been arrogant. As Henan governor he controlled the Six Armies and was made Grand Marshal; the great ministers of Tang all feared disaster and sought to escape—only Yicheng bound his heart to Congrong and sent his son to serve in the Prince of Qin’s household.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Congrong was proud. As Henan governor he held the Six Armies and the title Grand Marshal. Tang’s ministers feared ruin and tried to slip away—only Yicheng tied himself to Congrong and sent his son into the prince’s household.

sentences.zh: 明宗病，從榮謀以兵入宮，唐大臣朱弘昭、馮赟等皆以為不可，而義誠獨持兩端。

translations.literal: When Mingzong fell ill, Congrong plotted to enter the palace with troops. The great ministers Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun and the others all said it could not be done, but Yicheng alone held to both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong lay ill; Congrong planned to march on the palace. Zhu Hongzhao, Feng Yun, and the rest forbade it; Yicheng alone straddled both camps.

sentences.zh: 從榮已舉兵，至天津橋，弘昭等入，以反白，明宗涕泣召義誠，使自處置，而義誠卒不出兵。

translations.literal: Congrong had already raised troops and reached the Tianjin Bridge. Hongzhao and the others entered and reported the rebellion. Mingzong wept and summoned Yicheng to handle it himself, but Yicheng in the end would not lead troops out.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong’s troops reached the Tianjin Bridge. Hongzhao reported treason inside. Mingzong wept and told Yicheng to act—but Yicheng never marched.

sentences.zh: 馬軍指揮使朱弘實以兵擊從榮，從榮敗走，見殺。

translations.literal: The horse-army commander Zhu Hongshi led troops to strike Congrong; Congrong was defeated and fled and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongshi of the horse guard struck Congrong; the prince fled, was caught, and died.

sentences.zh: 三司使孫嶽嘗為馮赟言從榮必敗之狀，義誠聞而不悅。

translations.literal: The commissioner of the Three Departments Sun Yue had once told Feng Yun how Congrong was certain to fail. Yicheng heard and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yue of the Three Departments had warned Feng Yun that Congrong must fail. Yicheng heard and took offense.

sentences.zh: 及從榮死，義誠始引兵入河南府，召嶽檢閱從榮家貲。

translations.literal: After Congrong died, Yicheng at last led troops into the Henan prefectural office and summoned Yue to inspect Congrong’s household goods.
translations.idiomatic: After Congrong’s death Yicheng entered the Henan yamen with troops and called Yue to inventory the prince’s property.

sentences.zh: 嶽至，義誠乘亂，使人射之，嶽走至通利坊見殺，明宗不能詰。

translations.literal: When Yue arrived, Yicheng took advantage of the disorder and had a man shoot him. Yue fled to Tongli Ward and was killed. Mingzong could not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Yue came; in the chaos Yicheng had him shot. Yue ran to Tongli Ward and died. Mingzong could not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 義誠已殺嶽，又以從榮故，與弘實有隙。

translations.literal: Yicheng had already killed Yue and, because of Congrong, bore a grudge against Hongshi.
translations.idiomatic: Having killed Yue, Yicheng hated Hongshi for Congrong’s sake.

sentences.zh: 湣帝即位，弘實常以誅從榮功自負，義誠心益不平。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min took the throne, Hongshi often boasted of the merit of killing Congrong, and Yicheng’s heart grew still more unbalanced.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min enthroned Hongshi for killing Congrong. Yicheng’s resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 潞王從珂反鳳翔，王思同率諸鎮兵圍之，興元張虔釗兵叛降從珂，思同走，諸鎮兵皆潰。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu Congke rebelled at Fengxiang, Wang Sitong led the armies of the circuits to besiege him. Zhang Qianzhao of Xingyuan mutinied and surrendered to Congke; Sitong fled and the armies of the circuits all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Congke rebelled at Fengxiang. Wang Sitong besieged him with allied hosts. Zhang Qianzhao of Xingyuan defected; Sitong fled and the coalition broke.

sentences.zh: 湣帝大怒，謂朱弘昭等曰：「朕新即位，天下事皆出諸公，然於事兄，未有失範，諸公以大計見迫，不能獨違，事一至此，何方轉禍？

translations.literal: Emperor Min was furious and said to Zhu Hongzhao and the others: “I have newly taken the throne; the realm’s affairs all come from you gentlemen. Yet in serving my elder brother I have not lacked propriety. You gentlemen forced the great plan upon me—I could not stand alone against it. Affairs have come to this—how shall we turn disaster to fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min raged at Hongzhao and the rest: “I am new on the throne; you run the realm. I have not failed my brother in duty. You forced this plan on me. Now catastrophe is here—how do we turn it aside?

sentences.zh: 吾當率左右往迎吾兄，遜以位，茍不吾信，死其所也！

translations.literal: I shall lead my attendants west to welcome my elder brother and yield the throne. If he does not trust me, I shall die where I must!
translations.idiomatic: I will go west myself to welcome my brother and yield the crown. If he will not believe me, I die where I must.

sentences.zh: 」弘昭等惶恐不能對，義誠前曰：「西師驚潰，主將怯耳。

translations.literal: ” Hongzhao and the others were afraid and could not answer. Yicheng stepped forward and said: “The western army was startled and broke—its commander is only a coward.
translations.idiomatic: ” They were mute. Yicheng said: “The western host panicked because its general is a coward.

sentences.zh: 今京師兵尚多，臣請盡將以西，扼關而守，招集亡散，以為後圖。

translations.literal: The capital still has many troops. Your servant asks to lead them all west, hold the passes, gather the scattered, and plan what comes next.
translations.idiomatic: The capital still has strength. Let me take every man west, seal the passes, rally the fugitives, and plan again.

sentences.zh: 」湣帝以為然，幸左藏庫，親給將士人絹二十匹，錢五千。

translations.literal: ” Emperor Min thought it right, visited the Left Treasury, and personally gave each soldier twenty bolts of silk and five thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor agreed, opened the Left Treasury, and gave each soldier twenty bolts of silk and five thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 是時，明宗山陵未畢，帑藏空虛。

translations.literal: At that time Mingzong’s tomb was not yet complete and the vaults were empty.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong’s tomb was unfinished and the treasury bare.

sentences.zh: 軍士負物揚言曰：「到鳳翔更請一分。

translations.literal: Soldiers shouldered their goods and shouted: “At Fengxiang we will ask for another share.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers shouldered their pay and shouted: “We will demand another share at Fengxiang!

sentences.zh: 」朱弘實見軍士無鬥志，而義誠盡將以西，疑其二心，謂義誠曰：「今西師小衄，而無一騎東者，人心可知。

translations.literal: ” Zhu Hongshi saw the troops had no fighting spirit and that Yicheng was leading them all west. He suspected divided loyalty and said to Yicheng: “The western army suffered a small setback and not a single horse came east—the hearts of men are clear.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hongshi saw no fight left in them and feared Yicheng’s march west. He said: “A small defeat in the west, and not one rider comes east—the mood of the army is plain.

sentences.zh: 不如以見兵守京師以自固，彼雖幸勝，特得虔釗一軍耳。

translations.literal: Better use the troops at hand to hold the capital and secure ourselves. Though they may win by luck, they have only Zhang Qianzhao’s one army.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the capital with the men here. If they win, it is only Zhang Qianzhao’s host.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮之兵在後，其敢徑來邪！

translations.literal: The armies of the circuits are behind them—how would they dare come straight here!
translations.idiomatic: The other circuits are still behind them—they will not dare march on us!

sentences.zh: 」義誠怒曰：「如此言，弘實反矣！

translations.literal: ” Yicheng angrily said: “Words like this mean Hongshi has rebelled!
translations.idiomatic: ” Yicheng snapped: “Talk like that makes you the rebel!

sentences.zh: 」弘實曰：「公謂誰欲反邪？

translations.literal: ” Hongshi said: “Whom do you say wishes to rebel?
translations.idiomatic: ” Hongshi said: “Who do you call a rebel?

sentences.zh: 」其聲厲而聞。

translations.literal: ” Their voices were fierce and could be heard.
translations.idiomatic: ” Their shouts rang through the hall.

sentences.zh: 湣帝召兩人，爭於前，帝不能決，遂斬弘實，以義誠為招討使，悉將禁軍以西。

translations.literal: Emperor Min summoned the two men; they argued before him and the emperor could not decide. He then executed Hongshi, made Yicheng pacification commissioner, and sent all the palace troops west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called them in; they quarreled to his face and he could not judge. He killed Hongshi, made Yicheng pacification commissioner, and sent the palace army west.

sentences.zh: 湣帝奔衛州。

translations.literal: Emperor Min fled to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 義誠行至新安，降於從珂。

translations.literal: Yicheng reached Xin’an and surrendered to Congke.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng reached Xin’an and surrendered to Congke.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年四月，斬於興教門外，夷其族。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Qingtai he was beheaded outside the Xingjiao Gate and his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Qingtai 1 he was beheaded outside the Xingjiao Gate and his clan wiped out.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 五代為國，興亡以兵，而其軍制，後世無足稱焉。

translations.literal: The states of the Five Dynasties rose and fell through arms, yet their military institutions deserve no praise from later ages.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Dynasties lived and died by the sword, yet their military system wins no praise from later ages.

sentences.zh: 惟侍衛親軍之號，今猶因之而甚重，此五代之遺制也。

translations.literal: Only the title of the Personal Guard of the Palace Attendants survives today, still weighty—this is the legacy institution of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Personal Guard of the Palace Attendants still bears that name and still carries weight—a Five Dynasties legacy.

sentences.zh: 然原其始起微矣，及其至也，可謂盛哉！

translations.literal: Yet trace how it began in small things; when it reached its height, one may call it grand!
translations.idiomatic: It began in small steps; at its height it was truly grand.

sentences.zh: 當唐之末，方鎮之兵多矣，凡一軍有指揮使一人，而合一州之諸軍，又有馬步軍都指揮使一人，蓋其卒伍之長也。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang there were many frontier armies. Each army had one commander, and combining all armies of one prefecture there was again one overall commander of horse and foot—roughly the head of the rank and file.
translations.idiomatic: Late Tang swarmed with frontier armies. Each host had a commander; each prefecture’s hosts together had a horse-and-foot commander—the captain of the ranks.

sentences.zh: 自梁以宣武軍建國，因其舊制，有在京馬步軍都指揮使，後唐因之，至明宗時，始更為侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Liang built its state on the Xuanwu army and kept the old system: there was an overall commander of horse and foot in the capital. Later Tang followed this. By Mingzong’s time it was changed to overall commander of horse and foot of the Personal Guard of the Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Liang founded its dynasty on the Xuanwu army and kept the old form: a capital commander of horse and foot. Later Tang copied it. Under Mingzong the title became commander of the Personal Guard’s horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 當是時，天子自有六軍諸衛之職，六軍有統軍，諸衛有將軍，而又以大臣宗室一人判六軍諸衛事，此朝廷大將天子國兵之舊制也。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven had his own duties in the Six Armies and the various guards. The Six Armies had army commanders; the guards had generals. Again one great minister or imperial clansman was appointed to oversee the Six Armies and guards—this was the old system of the court’s great generals and the Son of Heaven’s national troops.
translations.idiomatic: The throne still kept the Six Armies and the guard offices, each with its commanders and generals, and again a great minister or kinsman oversaw them—the old court system for the emperor’s own hosts.

sentences.zh: 而侍衛親軍者，天子自將之私兵也，推其名號可知矣。

translations.literal: The Personal Guard of the Palace Attendants, however, was the Son of Heaven’s private army led by himself; from the name one can know it.
translations.idiomatic: The Personal Guard was different: the emperor’s private army, led by himself—the name says as much.

sentences.zh: 天子自為將，則都指揮使乃其卒伍之都長耳。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven himself was general, the overall commander was only the head of his rank and file.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the title of general, the overall commander was merely chief of his own soldiers.

sentences.zh: 然自漢、周以來，其職益重，漢有侍衛司獄，凡朝廷大事皆決侍衛獄。

translations.literal: Yet from Han and Zhou onward the office grew heavier. Han had a prison of the Palace Attendant Guard; all great court affairs were decided in that prison.
translations.idiomatic: From Later Han and Zhou the post grew heavier still. Han had a guard prison; great state matters were settled there.

sentences.zh: 是時，史弘肇為都指揮使，與宰相、樞密使並執國政，而弘肇尤專任，以至於亡。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Hongzhao was overall commander. With the chief councillor and chief councillor of the Bureau of Military Affairs he held state power, and Hongzhao was especially arbitrary—until ruin came.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao held the command and shared rule with the chief councillors and Military Affairs—yet Hongzhao ruled alone, down to ruin.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「涓涓不絕，流為江河。

translations.literal: The saying runs: “Trickling streams unceasing become rivers.
translations.idiomatic: They say: “Trickles that never cease become rivers.

sentences.zh: 熒熒不滅，炎炎奈何？

translations.literal: Tiny flames unquenched—how shall the blaze be stopped?
translations.idiomatic: Sparks that never die—how will you stop the fire?

sentences.zh: 」可不戒哉！

translations.literal: ” Is it not a warning!
translations.idiomatic: ” Take warning!

sentences.zh: 然是時，方鎮各自有兵，天子親軍猶不過京師之兵而已。

translations.literal: Yet at that time each frontier commissioner still had his own troops; the Son of Heaven’s personal army was no more than the capital’s troops.
translations.idiomatic: Even then each military governor kept his own troops; the emperor’s personal force was only the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 今方鎮名存而實亡，六軍諸衛又益以廢，朝廷無大將之職，而舉天下內外之兵皆屬侍衛司矣。

translations.literal: Now the frontier commands exist in name but not in fact; the Six Armies and guards are further abolished. The court has no post for great generals, and all troops within and without the realm belong to the Palace Attendant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Today the frontier commands are names without armies; the Six Armies and guards are gone. The court has no great field marshal, and every soldier in the realm answers to the Guard.

sentences.zh: 則為都指揮使者，其權豈不益重哉！

translations.literal: Then how can the overall commander’s power not grow still heavier!
translations.idiomatic: How could the commander’s power not weigh still more heavily!

sentences.zh: 親軍之號，始於明宗，其後又有殿前都指揮使，亦親軍也，皆不見其更置之始。

translations.literal: The title of Personal Guard began under Mingzong. Later there was also the overall commander of the Palace Front—also personal troops—and the record does not show when those titles were first changed.
translations.idiomatic: The Personal Guard title began under Mingzong. Later came the Palace Front commander—also imperial troops—and the books do not say when those offices were first refashioned.

sentences.zh: 今天下之兵，分屬此兩司矣。

translations.literal: Today the realm’s troops are divided between these two offices.
translations.idiomatic: Now the empire’s soldiers are split between those two bureaus.

sentences.zh: 藥彥稠

translations.literal: Yao Yanchou
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yanchou

sentences.zh: 藥彥稠，沙陀三部落人也。

translations.literal: Yao Yanchou was a man of the three Shatuo tribal groups.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yanchou came from the three Shatuo tribal groups.

sentences.zh: 初為騎將，明宗即位，拜澄州刺史。

translations.literal: At first he was a cavalry officer. When Mingzong took the throne, he was made prefect of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a cavalry officer. At Mingzong’s accession he became prefect of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 從王晏球破王都定州，遷侍衛步軍都虞候，領壽州節度使。

translations.literal: He followed Wang Yanqiu in breaking Wang Du at Dingzhou and was promoted to deputy commander of the palace foot guard and concurrent military governor of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Yanqiu against Wang Du at Dingzhou, then became deputy commander of the palace foot guard and military governor of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 安重誨矯詔遣河中指揮使楊彥溫逐其節度使潞王從珂。

translations.literal: An Chonghui forged an edict and sent the Hedong commander Yang Yanwen to drive out the military governor, the Prince of Lu Congke.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui forged an edict and sent Yang Yanwen of Hedong to expel the Prince of Lu Congke from his command.

sentences.zh: 以彥稠為招討使，明宗疑彥溫有所說，戒彥稠得彥溫毋殺，將訊之。

translations.literal: Yanchou was made pacification commissioner. Mingzong suspected Yanwen had been coached and ordered Yanchou that if he captured Yanwen he was not to kill him but would interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchou was made pacification commissioner. Mingzong suspected coaching and told Yanchou to take Yanwen alive for questioning, not kill him.

sentences.zh: 彥稠希重誨旨，殺彥溫以滅口，明宗大怒，然不之罪也。

translations.literal: Yanchou hoped to please Chonghui, killed Yanwen to silence him, and Mingzong was furious yet did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchou pleased Chonghui, killed Yanwen to seal his lips, and Mingzong raged but did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 長興中，為靜難軍節度使，党項阿埋、屈悉保等族抄掠方渠，邀殺回鶻使者，明宗遣彥稠與靈武康福會兵擊之，阿埋等亡竄山谷。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era he was military governor of the Jingnan army. The Tangut chiefs Amai, Quxinbao, and other clans raided Fangzhou and killed a Uyghur envoy. Mingzong sent Yanchou and Kang Fu of Lingwu to strike them jointly; Amai and the others fled into the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing he governed Jingnan. Tangut chiefs Amai and Quxinbao raided Fangzhou and killed a Uyghur envoy. Mingzong sent Yanchou and Kang Fu of Lingwu against them; the Tangut fled to the hills.

sentences.zh: 明宗以謂党項知懼，可加約束而綏撫之。

translations.literal: Mingzong thought the Tangut were now afraid and could be bound by treaty and soothed.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong thought the Tangut were frightened enough to accept restraint and peace.

sentences.zh: 使者未至，彥稠等自牛兒族入白魚谷，盡誅其族，獲其大首領連香等，遣人上捷。

translations.literal: The envoy had not yet arrived when Yanchou and the others entered from the Niu’er tribe into Baiyu Valley, slaughtered the whole clan, captured their great chiefs Lianxiang and others, and sent men to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy arrived Yanchou marched from the Niu’er tribe into Baiyu Valley, exterminated the clan, seized chiefs including Lianxiang, and sent word of victory.

sentences.zh: 明宗謂其使者曰：「吾誅党項，非有所利也。

translations.literal: Mingzong told his envoy: “I punish the Tangut not for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong told the messenger: “I strike the Tangut for no gain.

sentences.zh: 凡軍中所獲，悉與士卒分之，毋以進奉為名，重斂軍士也。

translations.literal: Whatever the army captures shall all be divided with the soldiers. Do not use tribute as a name to burden the troops again.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the army takes goes to the soldiers. Do not call it tribute and squeeze the ranks again.

sentences.zh: 」已而彥稠以党項所掠回鶻進奉玉兩團及遺秦王金裝胡錄等來獻，明宗曰：「吾已語彥稠矣，不可失信。

translations.literal: ” Before long Yanchou presented the jade the Tangut had plundered from the Uyghur as tribute—two pieces—and also the gold-mounted barbarian record the Prince of Qin had left behind. Mingzong said: “I have already spoken to Yanchou; faith must not be broken.
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon Yanchou sent up Uyghur jade the Tangut had seized and a gold-mounted barbarian register left by the Prince of Qin. Mingzong said: “I have told Yanchou—do not break faith.

sentences.zh: 」因悉以賜彥稠。

translations.literal: ” He therefore gave it all to Yanchou.
translations.idiomatic: ” He gave the whole lot to Yanchou.

sentences.zh: 又逐鹽州諸戎，取其所掠男女千餘人。

translations.literal: He also drove off the tribes of Yanzhou and took more than a thousand men and women they had seized.
translations.idiomatic: He also routed the Yanzhou tribes and recovered more than a thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 潞王從珂反，彥稠為招討副使。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu Congke rebelled, Yanchou was deputy pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Congke rebelled, Yanchou was deputy pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 王思同兵潰，彥稠與思同俱東走，為潞王兵所得，囚之華州獄，已而殺之。

translations.literal: Wang Sitong’s army collapsed; Yanchou fled east with Sitong, was taken by Congke’s troops, imprisoned in Hua prefecture, and later killed.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong’s army broke; Yanchou fled east with him, was caught, jailed at Hua, and killed.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖立，贈侍中。

translations.literal: When the Jin High Ancestor took the throne, Yanchou was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang posthumously made him Palace Attendant.
